text:
Kaapo Kakko is having the season people waited years for in New York. Sixteen points in 22 games, three points per 60 minutes, and the late winner against Anaheim on Nov. 23 with 2:25 left. After the 5-1 win over Vancouver on Nov. 19, Alison Lukan wrote that the "Kakko-Beniers-Samo line also cooked."

Here's the catch. He has 5 goals on about 3 expected (the quality of his chances), he's shooting 19.2% against a league norm near 13.5%, and Seattle has been finishing unusually well with him on the ice. His own shot volume is low; he's a passer first, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking shows 19% of his setups come from behind the net, more than double a typical forward.

The underlying game is real enough. Evolving-Hockey had him at 1.7 wins above replacement last season, mostly from even-strength offense, and the Kraken control more of the play with him on (+4.7 relative expected goal share at five on five). Our range for his season runs from 46 to 67 points. Watch the shooting percentage drift and see whether the assists cover it.
